About the AWP | Hyper Beast

High risk and high reward, the infamous AWP is recognizable by its signature report and one-shot, one-kill policy. It has been spray-painted using mesh fencing and cardboard cutouts as stencils. A predator is a predator, no matter the environment The AWP | Hyper Beast is a Covert-grade skin in Counter-Strike 2, featuring the Hyper Beast finish on the AWP. With a Covert rarity classification, it has approximately a ~0.26% chance of dropping from case openings.

How to Obtain: The AWP | Hyper Beast can be unboxed from the Falchion Case. It belongs to the Falchion Collection.

Float Value and Wear: This skin has a float value range of 0.00 to 1.00. This restricted float range means not all wear conditions are available, which can affect rarity and pricing for specific exteriors. Lower float values within each condition tier produce a cleaner in-game appearance and typically command higher prices.

Price and Market Trends: The AWP | Hyper Beast (Factory New) has a median market price of approximately $259.31, with the lowest listing prices available in the marketplace comparison below. The price has remained stable with minimal movement over the past 7 and 30 days, indicating balanced supply and demand. Across wear conditions, prices range from $35.75 (Well-Worn) to $259.31 (Factory New).

Community Rating: The AWP | Hyper Beast has a community rating of 4.3 out of 5 based on 200 votes. This above-average rating suggests the community considers it a solid choice among AWP skins.

Frequently Asked Questions

What's the difference between Factory New and Minimal Wear for the AWP | Hyper Beast?

Factory New (FN) AWP | Hyper Beast skins have float values between 0.00-0.07, showing minimal to no visible wear. Minimal Wear (MW) floats range from 0.07-0.15, with slight scratches or fading. The price gap between FN and MW varies by finish — some designs like the Hyper Beast pattern hide wear better than others, making MW versions a strong value alternative.

Is the AWP | Hyper Beast worth the price?

The AWP | Hyper Beast sits in the mid-to-high price bracket. It features a distinctive Hyper Beast design that stands out in-game and maintains good trading liquidity. It's part of the The Falchion Collection, obtainable from the Falchion Case, which adds to its collectible appeal. For players who main the AWP, this skin offers an excellent balance of visual appeal and investment stability compared to budget alternatives.

What is the float value range for the AWP | Hyper Beast?

Float values in CS2 determine a skin's wear level on a scale from 0.00 (perfect) to 1.00 (maximum wear). With a float range of 0.00 to 1.00, this skin has specific wear availability that affects pricing. Lower float values within any condition category (e.g., 0.01 vs 0.06 in Factory New) result in cleaner appearances and typically command higher prices. For high-value trades, always verify the exact float value using inspection tools.

Where is the cheapest place to buy the AWP | Hyper Beast?

Prices for the AWP | Hyper Beast vary across marketplaces due to fees, regional pricing, and seller competition. This skin can be obtained by opening the Falchion Case or purchased directly from third-party marketplaces. The Steam Community Market charges 15% fees, while third-party markets like Skinport, DMarket, and Buff163 offer lower prices with 2-10% fees. Is the AWP | Hyper Beast a good investment?

Investment potential depends on several factors. The AWP | Hyper Beast is from the The Falchion Collection (Falchion Case) — skins from discontinued collections tend to appreciate as supply decreases over time. Past performance doesn't guarantee future returns, but the AWP | Hyper Beast has maintained steady trading interest. Diversifying across multiple items typically reduces risk.

Can I use the AWP | Hyper Beast in competitive CS2?

Yes, all weapon skins including the AWP | Hyper Beast are purely cosmetic and can be used in all CS2 game modes including competitive matchmaking, Premier, and professional tournaments. Skins provide no gameplay advantages or disadvantages - they only change the weapon's visual appearance. Many professional players use skins during official matches, and you'll often see high-value items like this featured in tournament broadcasts.
